utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, kindly call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Today, let me greet the accused, the Defence counsel present in the courtroom. And good morning, Witness. Good morning, Mr. Scott. Good morning to your associates. Good morning, Ms. West. And good morning, Mr. Court Reporter assisting us, whose work is extremely difficult. Good morning to the Registrar and the usher. We have to complete Ms. Alaburic's cross-examination. I'll ask the legal officer to tell us how much time is left. And without further adieu, I'll ask Ms. Alaburic to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, I'm told that you have 13 minutes left. Try to remain within the next quarter of an hour so that Mr. Scott can start with his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, good morning to you. Good morning, Mr. Vegar. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. Vegar, shall we go back briefly to the topic of the foreign median their reporting. Tell me, to the best of your knowledge, did foreign media, such as agencies Reuters and AFB, have their own correspondents in Mostar or elsewhere in Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how they came by information about the events and developments in the area of Herceg-Bosna? Did they get their information by perusing domestic media, contacting local journalists, getting press releases from domestic institutions?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how they came by their information, mostly indirectly, except for the cases when they would come to Mostar themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, foreign reporters came to Mostar as a rule to prepare one story, one report, they would stay briefly, and then return to their base, or was it a different practice?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stayed briefly when they came, for an hour or two, several hours at most, and then they would go back.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In this way of work, when you are using other sources, is it possible for several media to publish one and the same story, based on one and the same source? For instance, if Reuters comes out with one story that contains a mistake, and other media take over the same story, can the same mistake be perpetuated in many reports?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If a mistake occurs and several media take over the story, then the mistake would be perpetuated.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, we spoke about the vertical and horizontal organisation. I just wanted to look at one more document, 2D 853. It's also a document of the Prlic Defence, 1D 1672.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. I did not want to interrupt, because we have little time, time is of essence, but I have a technical question because you were a journalist. Mention was made of foreign reporters. When they would go to Mostar, for instance, if they went at all, you seem to say that they would stay for very short periods of time. But when they went, did they meet with their colleagues, their Croatian colleagues, or did they go and have a whiskey at the hotel bar, and would they go back after gathering a few pieces of information from the hotel porter? You were a journalist, you were able to assess the work they would do. Was it serious, the work they did? Were they fast, efficient, or were just very superficial? How would you qualify their work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As we said previously, there were more than 2.000 reporters, many of them foreign, and you cannot lump them in the same heap. Others did their -- ones did their work very thoroughly; others would come, size things up in 10 or 15 minutes, and return to wherever they came from. The situation in Mostar was critical. Of course, when they would come, they would ask me for a statement, and then they would focus on the topic for which they came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last question. The major agencies, Reuters, AFP, did they have permanent correspondents in Mostar or were there reporters or journalists in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Their correspondents were mostly in Zagreb. When they came to Herzegovina, they would go to Medjugorje without going to Mostar at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And as part of their work, would they try and make contact with you? You knew them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, I knew those who came more than once. If they came only once, how would I know them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you would read their reports, were their reports objective or exaggerated? How would you qualify their reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What bothered me in their reporting was one-sidedness and their enslavement to their prejudice about what they called sides to the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And when you would observe inaccuracies in their reports, would you ask them to be corrected officially, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there was a factual mistake, yes. If it was an opinion expressed in the story, then I didn't think I had the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please, Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow me, another few follow-up questions on this that would not go against my 13 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Questions by Judges do not give you any more credit. It's part of your time. Otherwise, I won't ask any questions anymore, ever. If that is your purpose, I won't ask a single question anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Your Honour. We submitted a request to be decided about additional time for the Defence regarding Judges' questions. I'll proceed like this:

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, in Mostar did you receive AFP service, Reuters --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, you noticed that my questions were essential ones, that they really encapsulated the whole topic, so I fail to see what you could add to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would appreciate it if you allow me to finish, and then you will see my purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, President Antonetti asked you if you corrected information published in the foreign media. I would like to clarify for the Trial Chamber, what did you know at all about foreign reporting sitting in Mostar at the time? To begin with, did you receive Reuters, AFP, Associated Press Service, or other foreign agencies?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have that facility, but I had a certain insight into their reporting through the stories in the domestic media that were taken over from the foreign media.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So you did not know directly? You did not have direct insight into foreign reporting. You knew about those stories only if one of the domestic sources would refer to a foreign source?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: At that time in Mostar, did you have occasion to receive US, British, French weeklies and dailies, other publications, watch TV reports of foreign agencies reporting from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because of lack of time, I will skip the document I had called before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, regarding this question, does this mean that the HVO, in its civilian or military components, that nobody had a satellite dish able to receive, through satellites, CNN, Sky News, or other stations? There was nobody in Bosnia and Herzegovina with a dish capable of receiving foreign broadcasts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some people probably did, but we in the HVO did not have a service of that kind, nor did we have a person whose job it was to follow these programmes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You had individuals -- I suppose that if you had a Croatian worker who used to work in Frankfurt and had a second residence somewhere, he must have put a satellite dish in order to receive ZDF, a German channel, or not - I guess so - in order just to see the football matches of his local team. Wasn't it so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the HVO did not think it useful, in terms of media, to know what the world was saying about what was happening in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, that was important to us, but I'm telling you we did not have the technical facilities or the personnel who would do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, to follow up on this question, which I really believe to be very important, did you hear about the programme of the Croatian Television called "Picture Against Picture"? Some of those were presented here as evidence by the Prosecution. Did you hear about the programme?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Because of lack of time, I'll go on with leading questions. Is that a programme that portrayed reports by foreign television stations about the region of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, if you know, at that time was it one of the most popular programmes in all the areas covered by the Croatian Television signal?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was one of the reasons perhaps the fact that the overwhelming majority of citizens of the former Yugoslavia did not have satellite aerials and were not able to follow foreign programmes on their own?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the media isolation was rather bad.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now go back to the topic of my cross-examination. You told us, Mr. Vegar, and that was on page 31 of the transcript of the first day of your evidence, you said that you had several sources of information for your own work, employees of the IPD sector on all levels, then other sectors within the Defence Department, the Defence Department itself, and the Main Staff. Further on, you spoke a lot about the Main Staff as your source of information. I want some clarification here. Did you receive daily combat reports from the Main Staff? Daily combat reports, they were practically summaries of reports from all the operation zones, all the four of them?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, were they summary reports that the Main Staff also forwarded to other competent bodies in Herceg-Bosna, if you know?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know all the other recipients, but I received them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how and with what regularities did you receive information from other sources; for instance, from IPD personnel on other levels, that is, assistant commanders of units and operation zones?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received them, but I would have liked to have received more. They were rather irregular.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were they supposed to be daily, weekly, or on some other basis?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the operation zones, they were supposed to be daily. From other levels, depending on the importance of the events.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. What about other sectors of the Defence Department? From which sectors did you receive information, on what basis, and what kind of information?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was information relevant to the HVO, but also to the public, and it was much more seldom; for instance, the Health Sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you said that you used to receive information from the Defence Department itself, could you please explain what you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant information about the Defence Department itself, maybe from head of the Defence Department or some other people within the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I presume that I have still two more minutes. Let's hear some explanations about the college of assistants and heads of departments within the Defence Department. This is the last set of my documents. It is not important for me to discuss individual documents. P 05032, please take a look at it. P 05032, invitation from Bruno Stojic to you, Mr. Vegar, on the 14th of September, 1993, to attend the college session. And then the next document, P 05045, identical invitation to -- addressed to Slobodan Praljak. Please, Mr. Vegar, tell us whether you remember having received such invitations to attend college meetings.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I used to receive them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. Let's take a look at this document, and the document is P 04576 -- P 04756. These are minutes from a session of the college of the Defence Department. Yes, now the number has been correctly reflected in the transcript. This is the last document in this set of documents. At least this is how it's supposed to be. Please take a look at the first sentence. It says here, Head of the Defence Department drew attention to the fact that in the future, chief of the Main Staff should attend every college meeting. From this note, I conclude that the chief of the Main Staff did not attend every session of the Defence Department college. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose so, because I did not attend every session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It is important for us, Mr. Vegar, to determine very exactly what was the importance of such college sessions and whether members of the college took decisions from the purview of the Defence Department, and this is why I ask you whether you, as a member of the college, did take part in taking decisions which concerned SIS, military police, or the Main Staff, or any other segment of the Defence Department which would be outside your sector?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think that I did not have the right to take part in decision-making about other sectors.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, whether any other participants at such a session of the college had the right to decide on matters outside their purview?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Vegar. Your Honours, I believe that I've remained within the limits of the time that you allotted me. And if you allow me, I have one technical remark. General Petkovic Defence team submitted an objection to the list of evidence tendered by the Prosecution through the witness Buljan. Our objection was given an IC number, 926, IC 926. The objection referred to the lists coming from the Prosecution, which is P 924. Since the Prosecution rectified their IC list yesterday and specified the correct number of the document that they want to be approved, then the Defence team of General Petkovic has withdrawn their objection and the IC number can be then released for another evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Well, the Trial Chamber will check this later. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. It will take us a moment to distribute the binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, the binders have been distributed. Now you can begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And good morning to all of you, to each of Your Honours. Good morning to counsel. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vegar.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My name is Ken Scott. Sir, just to touch on this one topic very briefly again, in terms of your position, it seems that it's come up several times, but just to be absolutely clear: Beginning on approximately the 31st of January, 1993, you became the head of what we have described in this courtroom in the last couple of days as the Moral Guidance or Moral Education Sector of the HVO Department of Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sector for Moral Guidance, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And even though you did not receive an official appointment until sometime, I believe, around the 27th of August, there's no disagreement, I don't think, that from the end of January until sometime when you left, I believe in the summer of 1994, you continued in the position as head of that sector; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until 1993, towards the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, that will suffice for now. And there were times, if I understood your testimony, sir, in the last day or two, there were times where the terminology "IPD" might be used by you, perhaps by others, and in documents, to refer not only to the specific section by that name, but to what the -- the Department or Sector of Moral Guidance more generally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from the official title, Moral Guidance Sector, we used also the Information and Psychological Activities. That's IPD.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And at least until November of 1993, again just to be abundantly clear, your immediate superior, if you will, you would directly report to Mr. Bruno Stojic; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to touch again -- as the Chamber probably knows by now, I'm a bit of a stickler for locations, dates, and times, and I'd like to go to the question of locations. Counsel took you through, at one point, various locations of your offices and of the offices of the Department of Defence. If I heard you correctly, sir, I think I heard you say at one point that in the summer of 1993, the Department of Defence moved to some other building in Mostar, the one -- a different building than the one it had apparently occupied in the spring. Now, maybe I misunderstood, but sometime during the summer of 1993, the Department of Defence, including your office and Mr. Stojic's office, moved to another location in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was relocated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when was that, sir, and where? Where was the new location?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the summer of 1993, and the location was in Mostar, but further away from the delineation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm going to press you a bit more on both aspects. When you say the summer of 1993, do you recall whether it was in June, July, or August?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall specifically. Most probably in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you say you moved to another location in Mostar, can you help us as much as you can, sir, to give us the name of the building, the street address, the closest major intersection? Just assist us, please, as much as you can so that in future we'll know the location of that particular office.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm in two minds, whether -- do you ask me about locations where I was located or the Main Staff of the Defence Department? Which institution do you want me to tell you about?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Apologies to the interpreters. Let me come to those things in turn. At the moment, I'm talking about the Department of Defence in general. Well, when I say the "Department of Defence," the headquarters or senior management offices, if you will, if I can describe it that way, that included Mr. Stojic's office. So the question I'm asking you now is: In the summer of 1993, you've indicated that the Department of Defence moved its management offices. You think that was most likely in July. Can you give us, please, the approximate location of that office after you moved -- after the office moved in approximately July?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were locations found out of necessity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Sir. What we're looking for is the location, a street address, a building name, the closest major intersection. That's what I'm looking for, please.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at Cim, but I'm not sure. The settlement of Cim, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Can you spell that for the -- just so the record is very clear, when you say "Cim," in the transcript it's just been spelled C-i-m. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, C-i-m.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, let me turn to the second aspect you said a moment ago, which I had also intended to ask you. Now, did there also come a time, if I heard you correctly over the past couple of days, in the summer of 1993, where the offices of the IPD or the Morale or Moral Sector were at a location different than Mr. Stojic's office?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was on another location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When -- at what point did you move into two separate locations, where your office was at one location and Mr. Stojic was at a different location, approximately?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In circumstances when it was too dangerous to remain in the building that we used to occupy, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I haven't asked you the reasons why you moved. I've asked you about the location. When you did move, can you tell us when that was, when you went to a separate office than the one Mr. Stojic used, and the location of the moral guidance office once you moved to that location? Here I'm talking about date and location.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the date because I don't recall. I recall the location very well. It was on the avenue street, as it was called then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how far was that office, the office of moral guidance, at that point from where Mr. Stojic's office was at that time?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he later left -- the Defence Department left the building that I had left before, and they moved to a location maybe one or two kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, moving again to sources of education -- information, excuse me, as counsel was just talking about a few moments ago, you told us that at various press conferences and in the course of issuing press statements, you received -- on the one hand, you received, and then on the one hand you put out, if you will -- you distributed battle-field information. I think I heard you say something to the effect of casualty reports, et cetera. And my question again to you is: Where did you receive that information, talking about what was happening on a given battle-field, what the -- how many people had been killed, how many people had been wounded? Where did you receive that information?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And who, in particular, at the Main Staff? Because I'm going to ask you, in the course of the day, not just to tell us about the Main Staff generally, but I'm going to talk -- I want actual human beings. So you said you received it from the Main Staff. Who at the Main Staff did you receive the information from?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I could not get every time not -- to see the chief of the Main Staff or his deputy, but there was always somebody on duty at the Main Staff who provided that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the chief of the Main Staff or his deputy were available, I take it that you received your information from them, based on your last answer.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes, yes, but more often than not I did not receive it from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, here's what I'm going to suggest to you, sir, given just human nature and the way most organisations work: You were doing this on a regular basis, and I suspect, if you'll allow me, that there was someone there, there was a person you had more contact often than others; there was a person that you normally would pick up the phone on a daily basis or go across the street or whatever, a kilometre away, and collect information. So I'm putting to you, sir, there must have been some sort of a more or less regular contact person at the Main Staff. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such special person.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So if Mr. Praljak or Mr. Petkovic weren't available, then you just called a general number at the Main Staff, and whoever answered, that's who you talked to? Is that what the Judges should understand?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would either call or call on the Main Staff, but whoever was available at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, what is the problem?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, when my name is mentioned in terms of the distance between the Defence Department and the Main Staff, let it be precisely stated where the Main Staff was located while I was chief of Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I'm going to take a very active role in this, in terms of Mr. Praljak getting on his feet. If there's an objection, counsel can make legal objections. There's no reason for Mr. Praljak to make running commentary or give evidence by standing -- by popping to his feet whenever he feels like it, so I reject that participation. I'm not going to take direction from Mr. Praljak. If counsel -- if his counsel has a legal objection, then counsel can certainly state that, and I'll certainly do my best to be guided by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, you would receive, then, information from the Main Staff, and when you received this information from whomever you received it from, did someone have to essentially clear to you or indicate which information could be disseminated and which could not? And I'll take it further, sir. Normally, when there's an ongoing, for example, military operations, one does not disseminate all the detailed information about where certain troops are located, what your combat plans are, so who would tell you, when going in -- when you were walking into a press conference or preparing a press release, who told you, This information can go out, this information should, of course, remain confidential?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was clear yesterday when I said that nobody would specify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So you could get up, sir, or you could issue a press release and you could say whatever you wanted. You might divulge the -- you might divulge sensitive information, you might divulge the location of HVO troops that were in -- actually engaged in combat operations at the time, and no one would say, Well, that's not particularly helpful, sir, or that sort of information shouldn't go out? No one gave you that kind of guidance?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's turn to Exhibit P 00601. It will be probably in the first binder, please, if we have that, sir. And the binders will work essentially, I think, similar to what you've seen from the various Defence teams. They should be, hopefully, in numerical order, and to the extent there are Defence-marked exhibits, like 1D, or 2D, or what have you, those will be separately listed probably in the second -- the back of the second binder. P 00601. I believe you mentioned -- may have mentioned this the other day. Maybe I'm confusing it with another document by Mr. Rajic, but I think we might have looked at this. This is a document dated the 19th of October, 1992, from the Sector for Moral Guidance. It appears to have gone out under the name of Bozo Rajic when he was the head of that sector. I suggest to you, sir, and the Chamber that it provides a pretty good summary or overview of the work of that sector. Let me ask you to direct your attention, in particular, to the Roman numeral II, section Roman numeral II entitled "Work Plans, Methods and Means." Under item 1, "Information and Propaganda," it says: "Informing in units I see as a twofold and concurrent process: Incoming --" or excuse me, I'm sorry, "informing within units and informing the public. Both processes are of the same importance. The work should be carried out in such a way that the relevant facts, occurrences, observations, information, objections, suggestions, or requests are systematised two times a day at 1700 hours and 0700 hours, in principle, submitted to the higher level of the service, IPD, for compiling and submission, and then deliver the compiled information in the shortest possible time to the highest level of the IPD in the units so that the situation in the zone could be forwarded to the appropriate administration of this sector." Now, does that continue to be an accurate overview, if you will, statement, of the work of the IPD in that respect, both in October 1992 and throughout the time in 1993 that you were part of that organisation?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a -- describes an ideal situation which could not be realised in real life.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In this next paragraph, it says: "On the basis of the gathered reports, the Administration for Information makes a selection of the received information and decides which information, of what kind, and of which scope will be presented to the public through press conferences, announcements for public statements, commentaries, and other usual forms of public appearance." Sir, I asked you about that a few moments ago, and I suggested to you certainly there was some sort of screening or editing process which is described -- I put to you, which is described in the language I just to you a moment ago. Now, who, in the IPD section, would make those determinations?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, that is to say, while the assistant chief for moral guidance was Bozo Rajic, he did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And after Mr. Rajic departed, that became your responsibility?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, the language I just read to you, and I apologise that the paragraphs are not numbered, so it makes it a bit more difficult for me to assist you, but if you -- the language we were just reading a moment ago through press conferences, announcements, et cetera, if I can ask you to skip two paragraphs, and you should come to a paragraph that says: "Based on the collected and analysed information, the administration will issue a daily bulletin." And you said -- in among there -- and this also relates back to something counsel asked about a few moments ago, "... it would also contain other information related to activities, work, achievement of the units and the civil authorities, the highest bodies of the HZ-HB and the life of Croatian people." So what efforts can you tell me -- what information collection efforts, if you will, were engaged in to collect information from the highest bodies of the HZ-HB as part of your work and for distribution to the public and others?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you'll look in that paragraph I directed your attention to, skipping two paragraphs, it talks about also the collection and distribution of other -- other information, perhaps not strictly military or Department of Defence, but the civil authorities, including "the highest bodies of the HZ-HB." What information collection efforts were there by the IPD to collect such information for distribution to the public and others? Sir?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, we did not get the information. In fact, we did not receive the information from the highest bodies of the HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let's -- let's take that up in the context of the next language I'd like to point you to. In that same paragraph, several lines down, there is a sentence that continues on, saying this: "... bearing in mind that the essential points of the state policy, that is, the policy of the HZ-HB, be emphasised." Now, what state policy is being referenced here?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The state policy of Bosnia-Herzegovina, whose integral part was HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, in the parens, it says: "That is the policy of the HZ-HB." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, but I'm saying that it was the integral part of HZ-HB. In fact, HZ-HB was an integral part of the state policy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you had any question about the policy of the HZ-HB as it impacted the work of your section, albeit the larger section, Moral Guidance or IPD, how would you determine the policy of the HZ-HB in order that your work could be guided and could bear in mind at all times the essential points of that policy? How would you determine that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not need to determine that state policy every day. The policy was clear. Its basic principles were constant, and I adhered to that. I answered a specific question based on specific information and new facts that arose out of political talks, negotiations, agreements, international conferences led by the representatives of the three ethnic communities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So on those particular occasions where you did have a question -- so you didn't always have a specific because you kind of knew what it was, but when you did have a question, something came up and said, "Hmm, I wonder what the state policy is on that," who would you contact and go to for that information, to get an answer, to get guidance?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not contact anyone. I regularly followed, though, all reports, all the conclusions from all meetings, primarily of the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you make it sound as if you conducted the operations of this Moral Guidance Sector in a vacuum, in isolation, somehow just on your own. Now, I put it to you that simply can't be the case, sir. You had to take direction from your superiors, Mr. Stojic. You had to have collected information from other, as it says in this document, highest bodies of the HZ-HB. You simply weren't operating in a vacuum, sir. Who were some of the people that you turned to for that information?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, with full responsibility, that as far as political positions are concerned, I never sought out any -- anyone to provide me with interpretation. I always put out press releases and information based on something that already happened. I did not anticipate anything or make any judgements in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We saw, in the course of your testimony so far, some documents, and they were typically -- the ones we've seen so far have a date at the top. There would be a certain body of text, and following the text we would see the capital initial -- initials "V.V." Do you recall that? Do you recall documents like that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to admit I did not pay attention to this system of numbering of documents. I just looked for specific numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not sure how that got garbled, but maybe I'll try it again. Sir, we saw documents that were apparently produced by you or your section in the course of its business. They would typically have a date on the top of them. They would typically have a certain amount of text, and then they would be followed by the initials "V.V." And I'm saying "V.V." is your name, your initials, correct, "Veso Vegar"?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What were those kind of documents, how were they prepared, and what was the purpose of those particular kinds of documents?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the contents of the document. Mostly, those were press releases, statements made to some specific media.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And who drafted those statements that said "V.V." on them?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In most cases, me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's go forward to 2D -- it will be in the second binder, toward the back probably, sir, 2D 01353. If you have that, sir, this is a 21 September 1992 document over the name of Milivoj Petkovic, directed to the Defence Department. In the first paragraph, it says: "Following a request of the HZ-HB Government for a report on the implementation of the priority duties and tasks regarding the establishment of the HVO Main Staff," et cetera. Would you agree with me, sir, that this document was being specifically prepared at the request of the HVO HZ-HB so that it could be informed on the work of the Main Staff? Do you see the language, sir? Have I read it correctly?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if we go to paragraph number 7, toward the end of the document, over Mr. Petkovic's name, does it not say: "With regard to providing the information for the public, the GS," the Main Staff, "will forward reports of subordinated commands to the IPD department so that it can prepare information for the public." That information would have come to you or your section; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I see here, the Main Staff cedes reports, not makes reports, so the Main Staff makes the reports available.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to argue with you about that, sir. It would involve -- paragraph 7 makes reference to providing information to your operation, correct, IPD? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you please go next to Exhibit P 00518.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, just one minor detail. Under item 6 in this document, it appears that General Petkovic recalls that all the units in the HZ-HB territory are under HVO command. No other unit will be allowed to act independently. And then we have parentheses. The case is mentioned of the so-called Bregava Brigade. I have a question, therefore. What does that mean? Does this mean that the so-called Bregava Brigade was acting somewhat independently? Were you aware of that or not? If you weren't, just tell us so and we can move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the Bregava Brigade was the brigade at Stolac, but I really don't know that it acted independently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could go --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you could go, Mr. Vegar, to the next document, which is P 00518. This appears to be a report from Mr. Stojic to the HVO HZ-HB the very next day, on the 22nd of September, 1992. And, sir, if you can look at -- just scan through that document, please, and if you can recall generally what you saw in the previous document, which was the report from Mr. Petkovic to the Defence Department, and then we have this one, dated the next day, going from Mr. Stojic to the HZ-HB -- or HVO HZ-HB. Would you agree with me, sir, that essentially what Mr. Stojic passes on is largely, I'm not saying word for word - don't anyone suggest that I'm verbatim - but generally is passing on and incorporating the information received by -- from Mr. Petkovic the previous day; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, am I supposed to -- in fact, I would need to read the document before I answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We'll give you the time to take a look at -- to look at the document briefly. I'm not going to ask you in detail, but I'll suggest to you, and I'll suggest in the interests of time in the courtroom, that if you put the documents side by side, they're not the same, but they're very similar.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the similarity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, because our time is limited, sir, if I can just ask you to go to a section in the second document, the 518 document. In the English, it will be on the fifth page. In Croatian, sir, it will be the third paragraph from the end. So if you go to the last page or your last item above the date, and if you work at -- yourself up, please, to the third paragraph above, you'll see a paragraph that begins with: "The Moral and Propaganda Sector have begun holding press conferences every week on Tuesday and Friday." And we don't have the time to read the entire paragraph, but it talks about radio and TV, reviewing the newspapers on a daily basis, issuing press releases, daily monitoring and analysis of the newspapers. "We will issue denials, make comments, or start polemics about certain issues whenever we find it necessary." Now, again, does that, generally speaking, state at the time and continue to describe, at least in substantial part, the work of the Moral Guidance and IPD Sector?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the IPD was supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we can go next to Exhibit P 01593 in binder number 1, P 01593. You'll see that this appears to be an HVO document dated the 3rd of March, 1993, issued over the name of Mr. Stojic and yourself, Veso Vegar, directing the collection and provision of certain information. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "Submit the following documentation to the HVO Defence Department in Mostar: Film material; audio and videocassettes; photographs, books and war issues of newspapers," et cetera. "Your own and enemy propaganda material. Testimony by prisoners and detainees." When it makes reference to sending your own -- when you and Mr. Stojic directed these people to send your own and enemy propaganda material, what kind of material was that? Sir, I apologise but time is precious. Can you tell us, please, when you and Mr. Stojic said "send your own and enemy propaganda material," what material did you want them to send you?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their own material that they developed themselves. Let's focus on that. It didn't have to be something targeted at the enemy. It could have been the brochures that we distributed to the troops from the ICRC. It could have been information developed by IPD personnel for their own troops. But I don't believe they had any enemy material or targeting the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I think it is an interpretation problem. It says in the original "your own and enemy," enemy material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please start again, because there was a problem for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was about to say that it's the problem of translation, in fact, the translation of this document. In the original of the document, it says "your own and the enemy's propaganda material." It wasn't "your own enemy material."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The document appears to be correctly translated. I'm not clear -- not sure about the issue, but I appreciate counsel's effort to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, because again our time is limited or I would ask more questions about that, the next item that says "Testimonies by prisoners and detainees." Now, what did you and Mr. Stojic expect to receive in terms of testimonies by prisoners and detainees, and why were you collecting that information?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, by that I meant statements of people who had been in camps and information they could provide on how they had been treated there, and the people who had perhaps remained in the camps, how they were treated, what health condition they were in, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you'll go next, please, to P 02331 in the first binder, P 02331. Sir, this is a document that we've seen before, and I believe counsel may have used it again in the last day or two. It's dated the 12th of May, 1993, a communication from Mr. Petkovic to Mr. Stojic. And as counsel has previously pointed out, it's correct to say that the word "Order" on the middle of the first page should have been translated as "Request." There's no dispute about that. But what Mr. -- at least in terms of its going to Mr. Stojic, I mean. But what Mr. Petkovic is saying here is: "The IPD shall, based on reports and information received from all the operations zones, regularly and on time inform all HVO units about events in the territory of the community. "I suggest that this should take place at least once a day ..." Now, the information that's being collected here referenced by Mr. Petkovic. Can you confirm to us, sir, that it was some of that information, that kind of information, that would then find its way or come to you and to the IPD for the purposes of conducting your various work?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand this request by Mr. Petkovic like this: He believes that the IPD section should regularly and in a timely manner inform all HVO units, because I think he felt it wasn't being done properly, and that's why he suggested that at least once a day one summary report should be received by every unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But in producing the report, again, I guess the other side of the coin, so to speak, is the IPD would have to collect that information in order to prepare and distribute it; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it can only distribute information if it has information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Certainly. If you'll go, please, to Exhibit P 03274. P 03274 in the first binder. This appears to be a document coming from Mr. Stojic on the 7th of July, 1993, a rather wide distribution of 10 -- 10 items in the list, starting with "HVO Chief of Staff." And looking at the first paragraph, sir, do you agree with me that what this document does is Mr. Stojic says to all these people: "At its session on 5 July 1993, the HZ-HB HVO," that is, the HZ-HB government, "adopted a conclusion that all HVO bodies should submit their reports for the period between January-June 1993." Correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And below that, it says at one point: "The following officers are responsible for the implementation of this conclusion: HVO Chief of Staff Petkovic...," the assistant heads, the chief of the Military Police Administration, the chief of the Personnel Department and others? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when such information projects were underway, it did often -- often also involved IPD, given the information business that you were in, that part of the information to prepare such reports would come from IPD?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I want to -- the courtroom will see that -- I think we saw most, if not all of these next couple of documents previously, but I'd like to revisit them briefly again. If you can turn, please, to 2D 00687 in the second binder, 2D 00687. Sir, this is a document dated the 24th of November, 1992, over the name of Mr. Petkovic. I'm going to paraphrase it, if I might be allowed. Everyone in the courtroom will have it. But again as I think we saw before, it's Mr. Petkovic's attempt to impose controls on contacts with the media and information going to the media; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an attempt by Mr. Petkovic to prevent out-flow of confidential information and provision of information by people who would not be authorised to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And item 3, in particular, specifically says: "Press conferences are responsibility of the Defence Department's IPD (Information and Propaganda). All others within the zones, headquarters, and formations can organise conferences based upon my permission." Now, when it refers to the Defence Department IPD, that's your section; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you can go to Exhibit P 00797 -- well, I'll tell you what. Hopefully, this -- we'll skip them in order, because -- since you're closer to the next one, to try to assist you in the courtroom. If you can turn while you're in the second binder to 2D 00637. It should be close by. 2D 00637. This a document dated 20 September 1993, over the name of Slobodan Praljak: "I command: All informations for the media about the situation at the battle-field will be exclusively approved by the Public Relations officer from HVO main staff --" excuse me, it doesn't staff, "HVO main headquarters," and among others it's distributed to Mr. Veso Vegar; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, addressed, delivered to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry. Is this not again a similar attempt by Mr. Praljak to impose, what I'll suggest, pretty strict control on contact with the media by the HVO; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have an objection for misinterpretation of this document. It is clearly seen from this document that it goes for information about the situation in the -- at the battle-field that doesn't concern other contacts with the media, so I'd like to ask my learned friend from the Prosecution to be precise in describing this document and its character.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think I just read it in full a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, it's an effort to control the distribution of such information quite strictly, isn't it? One person, apparently, exclusively approved by public relations officer of the HVO main headquarters; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that many things are not clear to me regarding this command, this order, the fact that public relations officer of the Main Staff of the HVO is authorised to give information to the media about the situation on the battle-field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, isn't there a very classic conflict here in this document between those who are on the ground and those who are sitting comfortably in their offices? Those on the ground seek to control media information, and this is a document coming from Mr. Praljak. It is a very clear document. It says that all the information has to be approved by the public relations officer from the main headquarters, and you are one of the addressees for information. If you compare this document with other documents from the Defence Department, you can see that here there is a conflict in terms of power or competence. What do you think of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when you mentioned people on the ground, let me, please, to finish my answer about the locations of the Main Staff and the Defence Department. I mentioned just one location, asked by the Prosecutor, where we went to when we left the main or the original locations. There are two other locations of the Main Staff, and this is why Mr. Praljak intervened as he did. One was five or six kilometres away from the original one, and the next at twenty kilometres away in the town of Citluk. And after -- shortly afterwards, the date of this command, the location was 50 kilometres away, and I believe that this is something the Chamber should know. I can't remember exactly. This is September 1993, autumn. I believe that the Main Staff was reorganised around that time, but don't hold me to that, and maybe this order is based on that reorganisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your explanation comes from the fact that locations were changed, and you date that back to the month of September. Very well. It's been recorded. The time has come to have a break. Mr. Scott, a 20-minute break. We shall resume then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're resuming our session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, we were looking at 2D 00637 a few moments ago, and I want to come back to that in a moment. But before we get too far ahead, I'd like to go back and ask you to look at P 00797, which is in the first binder, P 00797. This is a document which again I think we saw, but dated the 24th of November, 1992, over the name of Milivoj Petkovic, ordering, and again I'll paraphrase, that any contact be had with UNPROFOR and the European Community members only with the permission by the chief of the HVO Main Staff. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, before going on to other points, wouldn't you agree with me that when we look at the three documents we've last looked at, 2D 00687, Mr. Petkovic's 24 November order about control over information going to the media, this one, P 00797, and 2D 00637, the September order by Mr. Praljak that we were also looking at a moment ago, there was an effort from the top down to control the information going out to the media and to the international agencies; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it goes for a desire to systematically order the area of information provision and not control in terms of prohibition.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you'll turn back to -- and I'm sorry to -- to everyone in the courtroom, but we'll need to go back, please, to 2D 00637, the Praljak order in the second binder, because there's a second point that I'd like to address, please. 2D 00637. Now, again, what Praljak says here is all information about -- "All information for the media about the situation at the battle-field will be exclusively approved by Public Relations officer from HVO Main Headquarters." Now, who was the public relations officer at HVO main headquarters who would exclusively approve this information going to the media?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at the Main Staff or generally in the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, this document, I'm reading -- you have the document in front of you. I've read it now to you twice. It's very short.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "Public Relations officer from HVO Main Headquarters," so who was that, when Mr. Praljak issues such an order referring to such a person?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, the only other individual that's copied by name on this document is Veso Vegar. You see that, don't you? Yes?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to put to you quite directly that at least for most of 1993, if not all of it, you really were that person, weren't you? You wore both hats, if you want to put it that way? You were the spokesperson for the Department of Defence and the spokesperson for the HVO Main Staff, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was just the spokesperson for the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Tell us, sir -- give us the name of the person who fulfilled that function at the HVO Main Staff, if it wasn't you.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really can't recall. I don't recall who that person was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I put it to you again, sir, that the reasons you were saying earlier today that perhaps journalists might perhaps attribute to you the position as spokesman for the Main Staff, or spokesman for the Department of Defence, or spokesman for the HVO, is because, in fact, you did wear all those hats, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Journalists attributed to me all those duties and posts, and for the main part the reason for that is their ignorance of the structures of the Defence Department and the HVO and the military structure. They very frequently mistook the Main Staff for the Defence Department and thought it was one single body, which was not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During 1993, sir, in terms of the regional media, that is, the media in the former Yugoslavia, Bosnia, Serbia, Croatia, et cetera, in terms of the regional media, who were your principal media contacts in carrying out your function as head of IPD and Moral Guidance?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, all correspondents who worked out of Mostar and Herzegovina, meaning correspondents of the media based in Sarajevo, they were the most numerous. Then media correspondents from the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let me come back to some of those individual ones in a moment. I'm not sure if we've explicitly, at least, referred to or clarified this. In some of the documentation over the past couple of years, the courtroom has seen references to HINA, H-I-N-A. That is the state press agency of the Republic of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And we may have seen or may see yet today a reference to something called Habena, H-a-b-e-n-a. That was the public agency, news agency, press agency, if you will, of Herceg-Bosna; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was the news agency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was the director of Habena?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Bozo Rajic was either the director or editor-in-chief, but he was there in Habena.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did that continue to be the case after Mr. Rajic left the position as head of Moral Guidance, that you then took over, and did he then go and become head of Habena at that time?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Habena did not exist at the time, only after a couple of months while he was minister of defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, and then after a couple of months from that date, the Habena agency was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So when you say "a couple of months," we're talking sometime in March or April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to my learned friend. There is a mistake. Like the day before yesterday, I would like the witness to state which position Mr. Bozo Rajic occupied when he left the post of the assistant to the head of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He went to occupy the post of the minister of defence of the Croatian Community of Bosnia-Hercegovina -- Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Counsel -- Your Honour, I'll clarify and ask. There's no dispute that Mr. Rajic left for a time and became the minister of defence of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That's correct, Counsel?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, my learned friend. The witness's answer is incorrect two times in a row, so an impression is gained that he is not -- doesn't know what he's talking about in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There won't be a dispute about that, at least from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if I can go back to the agencies -- not the agencies, the outlets, if you will, which -- we are talking about the regional media and you mentioned Sarajevo and you mentioned Croatia. Can you give us the names a few -- name a few of the -- like, for instance, the newspapers, the regional newspapers that you had most of your contacts and dealings with ? And in the interests of time, sir, let me suggest, did that include "Vecernji List," did it include "Slobodna Dalmacija"? Did it include "Vecernji"?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, "Oslobodjenje" and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "Oslobodjenje" in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in terms of television, television stations, did that -- was your principal contact -- did it include, at least, Croatian TV, sometimes abbreviated HTV?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, among others.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were there any other radio stations -- excuse me, television stations that you had more frequent or regular dealings with others -- other than Croatian TV?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: When technical circumstances allowed, Television Sarajevo would work out of Mostar every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And as far as radio stations, would it be fair to say your principal dealings were with Radio Herceg-Bosna in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After its establishment in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Approximately when in 1993, sir, approximately?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember precisely. The autumn 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We'll see a document that will give us that in a moment. And any other radio stations, apart from Croatia Radio, Herceg-Bosna, any other radio stations that you had, again, more regular or more frequent dealings with the connection with your work?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, two radio stations in Mostar, Radio Sarajevo, Radio Zagreb, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The two other stations in Mostar, can you give us the names, please?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: One was Radio Mostar. And it's a radio station that had existed before the war in Mostar. And the second and newly-established War Studio of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The so-called War Studio was, if you will, the alternative radio station established by the Muslims sometime during 1992/1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Because of the clarification on Mr. Rajic's position, I'm reminded that we didn't actually get an answer on the question about Habena. You had indicated that that was formed, I think you said, approximately two months after Mr. Rajic left his position at the HVO Department of Defence, and I was suggesting to you at the time of the -- we went into the clarification, two months would mean, then, that Habena was formed sometime in approximately March or April of 1993; is that correct? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was later than that. I believe it was towards the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, again, perhaps we'll see documents that will assist us. Your initial answer was that it was a couple of months after Mr. Rajic ceased being the head of the Moral Guidance Sector, which was in January, but let's go on. Now, I've asked you about the regional media, and let me ask you about international media. I take -- would it be fair to say that two of your principal electronic media contacts were with, for example, CNN, BBC; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No? How about newspapers?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, there were hundreds of foreign journalists. I cannot highlight the main ones, so to speak. There was "Daily Telegraph," "The Guardian," "Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung," "Sky News," among -- ITN among TV stations, then CNN and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Rajuno."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for assisting on that. Let me show you, just a -- very briefly, a video-clip, P 02157, which I think we can play in Sanction, P 02157. It's very short, but just to illustrate the kind of press conference or appearance that might have occurred at the time. This is from May 1993, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Go back to the beginning of it. It's fairly short.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "The battle is being fought in the centre of Mostar, said a co-op military spokesman who blamed the conflict on Muslim units who had come to Mostar from Eastern Bosnia, upsetting the ethnic and military balance."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can we go back, please, can we go back to the beginning and -- please. Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, is that you giving a press conference in about May 1993 on CNN or to CNN?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Since it's so -- just can -- now that we've -- can you just play that again very briefly?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "The battle is being fought in the centre of Mostar, said a co-op military spokesman, who blamed the conflict on Muslim units who had come to Mostar from Eastern Bosnia, upsetting the ethnic and military balance."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, was it also part of the information effort, if you will, information propaganda, I take it, each side would try to monitor the media communication -- media contacts and communication of the other side; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to remind you again of the technical limitations we faced in following the work of the other side. Of course, in wartime you always want to hear what the other side thinks and tells, but my technical facilities for monitoring that, and even the time, were limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's go to Exhibit P 08115 in the second binder, P 08115. Sir, this appears to be a report or a note from the SIS on the 25th of March, 1994. Subject: Monitoring of the Mostar Radio War Studio broadcasting. Now, you confirmed for us just a few moments ago that the Radio War Studio was the Muslim radio in Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the radio station of the 4th Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you and your office, the IPD, in various documents I think we showed this, sir, you worked quite closely from time to time with SIS, the intelligence agency, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And they were one -- but they were one of the organisations from which you received information; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Very rarely, though, because that's a service that gathered intelligence information, secret information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, why would the SIS, to your understanding -- why would the HVO authorities want information about the Mostar Radio War Studio's coverage of who the Muslim side considered to be the most notorious perpetrators of crimes against detained Muslims? Sir, why would the authorities want to know this information? Please.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that all authorities want to know what other media are saying about them; in this case, the other side, the enemy side.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe it would be a good idea if the Prosecutor first asked Mr. Vegar about the position where he was when this report was made, and then we'll see if he was in a position to know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if we can go to Exhibit P 0 -- excuse me, P 10627, P 10627, which will be in the second binder. P 10627. Sir, this is a report concerning the work of Croatian Radio Herceg-Bosna, dated the 27th of September, 1993, and if you look at the document, I think in the second paragraph on the first page, I think you'll see then this -- relating to one of the questions we discussed earlier, the broadcast of the programme started a month before the anticipated dead-line, i.e., on 14 May, 1993. So does that refresh your memory as to when Croatian Radio Herceg-Bosna went on the air?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I thought I remembered it was a bit later, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And if you can please go -- if you'll go to find, by way of a landmark, if you will, to paragraph 6. I'm not going to ask you about paragraph 6, but if you can find paragraph 6. And for the English speakers or readers, the second -- page 3, second paragraph. Sir, you should find a paragraph that starts with these words: "The total programme orientation, editorial policy, and programme scheme ..." Tell me when you have found that, please. The first paragraph under paragraph numbered 6: "The total programme orientation ..." Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "The total programme orientation, editorial policy, and programme scheme are defined by the basic documents of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, with an emphasis on presenting the survey of the activities of the official bodies," HVO Main Staff, soldiers, refugees, et cetera. Skipping down one sentence: "One can state that the defence of the area of Herceg-Bosna is very much present in the programme of the Croatian Radio of Herceg-Bosna through the statements issued by the Main Staff." That's a fair description of the work of the radio station, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there's a mistake here. There were no press releases from the Main Staff. It's repeated again, this confusion that I mentioned between the Main Staff and the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, sir, this isn't a foreign journalist. This is an HVO document. That's apparently what Mr. Srecko Vucina, management board of the radio station, apparently thought that they were issued by the Main Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the name of the author of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you look at the last page, sir, I think you'll see Mr. Vucina's name, and another name, Zlatko Prlenda. But in any event, sir, the paragraph I just referred to --

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it could be Zlatko Prlenda, because he was the director of the radio, but this radio was not part of the military structure of the HVO or the Defence Department, where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The next paragraph, sir, you will see -- the one that we just referred to, it says: "One should particularly single out the fact that a large number of information from all battle-fields, as well as the information from Herceg-Bosna in general, have been broadcast to the whole world by the London BBC (which takes over the Croatian Radio of Herceg-Bosna's news programme one to four times a day ..." And then also goes on to talk about the cooperation and distribution through HINA, the Croatian state news agency. Those are both correct statements, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, BBC certainly took over some programmes, for a long time even after the war, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask you, please, to turn to Exhibit P 05551, 5551, just ever so briefly. Sir, this is the record of the minutes -- the English translation is wrong on the date. It should be the 1st of October, 1993, rather than "March," and the date under the -- in the phrase "convene" should also say "on 4 October 1993." I apologise for the error. But, sir, in reference to the document we were just looking at, if you look in this agenda, item number 9, I think that you will see that Mr. Jadranko Prlic had put, as agenda item 9: "An examination of the report on the performance of work and task to establish and set in operation Croatian Radio Herceg-Bosna," which is the report which is marked as Exhibit P 10627 that we were just looking at. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, when we were -- when we first began your testimony on Monday, and you were questioned about what you were doing, your profession as a journalist, I think it was one of the Judges, perhaps it was the President, but in any event you were asked about what you were currently doing, and I believe at one point you said -- you were talking about being a journalist, but you said you were retired? Did I hear you correctly or is that a misunderstanding?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And so do we understand correctly, sir, that you're not presently involved in any -- engaged in any form of employment or means of making a livelihood?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No regular income, except for my pension.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
