utterances.text: And do you have irregular sources of income, then; consulting fees, work on behalf of political parties, media consulting?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have compensation, but I work as a consultant and I am engaged in a political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What kind of consulting work do you do?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lead an office in a political party, the information office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what political party is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How long have you been involved with that party, sir?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What political party were you involved in prior to that, prior to approximately 2007, two years ago?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not work in political parties before, but I worked in the electoral campaign of the HDZ BH in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And were you a member of that party, sir?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you a member of the HDZ party in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm still -- I'm just a little curious, sir, because on the first day of your testimony, you gave what Judge Trechsel also observed was a rather odd and qualified answer. When you were asked about whether you had ever been a member of the HDZ, you said: "If you mean the BiH, my answer is no." And to my way of thinking, sir, you never really gave a clear answer of what you meant by that. So if you were not a member of the BiH, were you a member of some other political party at that time?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now I am a member of the HDZ 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How about in 1993/1994?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a member of any political party then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, now let's be clear here, because a few moments ago you made the distinction between being a member of a party and working for a party. So in 1993/1994, maybe you weren't the member of a party, but were you engaged in activities in connection with -- on behalf of a party? Did you work for a political party at that time?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't want to play word games with you, sir, about whether it was employment or something else. Were you associated with a political party in 1992, 1993, 1994, in any aspect?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I put to you that you've worked quite hard these last few days to portray yourself as something of a technocrat, but the reality is, sir, you've been closely and actively involved in Croat nationalist politics since at least 1992, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not involved in Croat nationalist politics, and at the time of the war and in the post-war years, I was not a member of any political party. If you ask me about party activities, I was a member of the HDS party from 1990, when HDS was established in Zagreb, and then in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but with the end of the war this party ceased to exist, it stopped to be active and is not active today, so that in that year, my party activities ceased.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When did you obtain your Croatian citizenship?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, one minor problem. Line 2 on page 47, you said that you were a member of the HDZ in 1990, and now, on line 22, page 47, you said that you were a member of a party called "HDS."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can be allowed -- if I can be allowed to assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, is it "HDZ" or "HDS"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] HDS. I was a member of that party in 1990.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. The answer of the witness was not recorded in full. The witness said that in 1991, his engagement, even in that party, ceased. I think that should be on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can I also -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I also clarify, Witness. Perhaps this may be a source of confusion; maybe not, but let me try. When you say you were a part -- you were a member of a party, HDZ 1990, that's the name of the party; correct? It's not the date of your membership. There is a political party now in Bosnia-Herzegovina called "HDZ 1990"; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you said a moment ago that you obtained your Croatian citizenship in 1993. Can you tell the Judges how you made your application and where you submitted your application for Croatian citizenship? Was that in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in Mostar, but I don't really remember. And if I applied, I didn't apply only for myself, but for my family as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And going back to your political involvement, you say -- you say you haven't been a member of HDZ, but Mr. -- there's a man named Mr. Jelavic who has been an actively involved, one of the leaders of that party in the second half of the 1990s; correct, Mr. Jelavic?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you have been, at various times, a very close adviser and associate of Mr. Jelavic, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You were -- did you receive payment from Mr. Jelesic or -- Jelavic, excuse me, or the party for the work that you did?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. But just so we can be clear here, because that goes back to why I was asking these questions a few minutes ago, sir: So you've told the Judges and you've left the impression that you haven't been associated with the HDZ, and yet you were an adviser to the leader of the party, weren't you? Correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and there were other people, his advisers, that were not members of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, when you left your position at the Department of Defence and went to work to "Slobodna Dalmacija," in about December of 1995 you conducted an interview with a man named Vladislav Pogarcic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, because I did many interviews. Maybe with him too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's look at Exhibit P 08623 in the second binder, P 08623. 08623. It should be in the second binder. If it's not, can we go to e-court, please, to try to save time, please. My apologies if there's a problem. Sir, while we're looking for that, I'll represent that -- the Chamber has seen this before. It won't be new to the courtroom. It is an interview that you apparently conducted while employed at "Slobodna Dalmacija," an interview on the 9th of December, 1995, with Mr. Pogarcic. Now, because our time again is so limited, I would like to direct your attention and I'll direct the courtroom's attention in the English version in the -- toward the bottom of the second page. And, sir, if you can find a paragraph -- you asked a question -- you'll see that there's references to the questioner and the speaker. So you'll see -- you'll see: "Vegar, Pogarcic, Vegar, Pogarcic." So if you find one of the "Vegar" entries where you say -- you put this question to Mr. Pogarcic: "Do you really think that the peaceful division of Bosnia is possible?" Do you see that? Do you see it, sir? "Do you really think that the peaceful division of Bosnia is possible?" Vegar.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that question on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. We'll just have to keep scrolling, I guess, unless can we get anything else as a reference? It's probably roughly halfway through the overall document in most formats, I would think. Or no, I'm sorry, I wouldn't -- well, probably not. Let me read this to you, sir, and I'll read slowly and for translation, and I'm sure that the courtroom will correct me if I'm wrong. You put that question to Mr. Pogarcic, and Pogarcic says: "Yes. In fact, that possibility is the only clear result of these four years of war. Remember how Bosnia was described at the beginning of the war as a 'leopard skin.' Today, however, it is a country of three ethnic communities, each having its own strictly-delineated territory. This might be thought to be ugly, there are people who are even disgusted by this, but they should know that it is the result of the will of the population itself. The Serbs, Muslims, and Croats have ethnically cleansed territories wherever they could (meanwhile, it must not be forgotten that the Pandora's Box of ethnic cleansing was forced open by the Serbs, although the two other nations could not resist the temptation to take a look into it), until they reduced the members of the other ethnic communities to 10 per cent or less of the total. With 10 per cent or less of the total, one cannot threaten the political position of the majority, while simultaneously the minority functions as an ornament and can even serve as proof of the will to create a 'multiethnic society.'" My question to you, sir: Did you share that same view as Mr. Pogarcic in those statements?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, as a journalist, do not necessarily have to share political views, the political views of the person I'm interviewing. I would not agree with all these statements by Mr. Pogarcic, but I recorded them, as he said that. At that time, he was deputy foreign minister of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I thought it was important for the readership to hear his thinking, and that's why I conveyed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apology. In the early part of the passage that I read to you, let me just break it down into some smaller pieces, Mr. Pogarcic suggests that the division of Bosnia was "the only clear result of these four years of war." Do you agree with that statement?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The war ended with the peace agreement that divided Bosnia and Herzegovina into two entities. If that's what he meant, then he's right. All the rest are very debatable theories about ethnic cleansing, the percentage of an ethnic community can have in an area without threatening the other ethnic community. That maybe derives from something he read. But, again, I have to say I don't have to share his positions, because I'm not writing a commentary here. It was an interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's correct. You don't have to, you're absolutely right, but my question is whether you do, in fact. And, for example, do you agree with the statement that all the three ethnic parties, the Serbs, the Muslims, and the Croats, all three had engaged in ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you believe the Serbs engaged in ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you believe the Muslims engaged in ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a consequence of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you believe that the HVO, the Croats -- excuse me, the Croats - to follow through with Serbs, Muslims, and Croats - do you believe that the Croats engaged in Muslim -- in ethnic cleansing, excuse me?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So everyone did, except for the Croats; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may. The Prosecutor showed a passage to the witness, and we don't have the document in the binder; neither does the witness. But when he highlights the question by the witness, is peaceful division of Bosnia possible, had the witness been in a position to read the article, he would have read the previous answer which preceded that question, and this was taken out of context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, would you mind reading, in your own language, the sentence starting with "Zar mitlite"? Read in your language the question there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Do you believe that a peaceful division of Bosnia is possible?" Do you mean the question or should I read on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just the question. I ask this, because in the text as translated into English, we have "Really," so does that mean -- it seems as though it meant, "Do you really think that?" So in the English translation, it's more as a question. But the way you put the question in your language -- as you read it in your language is, you don't have this qualification; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking a question and putting forward a thesis in that question which was present in the public domain then and now. The question of the public and the readership was that it was impossible for Bosnia to be divided in a peaceful manner, so I'm asking this individual, Do you really think that a peaceful division of Bosnia is possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if we could move off this document to P 10826, also in the second binder, P 10826. Sir, this is an article -- a media article from Agence France-Presse from the 3rd of March, 2001. In the third paragraph, it says this: "Veso Vegar, an adviser to leaders of HDZ, the main nationalist Croat Democratic Union, told Friday that an inter-regional council made up of areas with a Croat majority would probably be set up, such a council would have its own parliament and government, he said." Do you remember giving interviews like that around this time, March 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time I did issue statements to the press.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And at the end, the very last paragraph of this particular article, says: "The Croat member of Bosnia's Presidency, Ante Jelavic, who also heads the HDZ, also said Wednesday that the federation was 'a Muslim entity without Croats,' and the government was 'illegal and illegitimate and we will no longer either participate or recognise it.'" My apologies, apologies to the interpreters for being so quick. Shall I repeat any of it? I think it's -- thank you. And did you agree with Mr. Jelavic on that assessment, that the current government structure at that time was, quote, "illegal and illegitimate" and the HDZ would no longer either participate or recognise it?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I have to provide a wider explanation. We are entering a political debate. Such statements and such assessments issued by Mr. Ante Jelavic then have been repeated all those years since 2001 to date. They were deeply founded sometimes --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise to you, sir. If my time was not more -- less limited, I would certainly be happy to get a longer answer, but my question to you is: Do you agree? Do you share the assessment stated by Mr. Jelavic in this article?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object. I do believe that the witness should be allowed to explain why this happened. If this is not allowed to him, then it's impossible for him to answer in the way that the Prosecutor wants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Listen, Ms. Nozica. If the Prosecutor puts the question in an infelicitous way, too bad for him. Don't try to rescue him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, let me --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can explain this statement. It is short, it's taken out of context of the overall discourse of Mr. Jelavic. At that moment, and this was not solely Mr. Jelavic's opinion, the government did not include representatives of the strongest Croatian political party which was voted for by 70 per cent of the Croatian voters at the time, so that party and the people represented by that party did not have a representative in that government of the time, the HDZ BiH. So the HDZ BiH did not have any representatives in the federal government, a political party which reached 70 per cent of the Croatian vote in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The federal government was established then, which included ministers, representatives of some Croatian political parties, who received 29 votes in total in that election.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise to -- excuse me. I apologise to the courtroom, but I don't have time, unless the Chamber wants to give me more time to get into how many seats each of the parties won during these particular elections. Now, let me go on, sir, to some other documents and perhaps it will clarify these issues. I'll be happy to address it further if the time is provided for me to do so, but there is no such time at the moment. And I apologise to you, Mr. Vegar, for that. But if you could please turn to Exhibit P 10828, P 10828. It should be very close by, the same binder. Sir, around this same time in February 2001, do you recall supporting the possibility of actually withdrawing the credentials of two international diplomats, including the US ambassador to Bosnia and the head of the OSCE mission to Bosnia, because of their concerns about certain anti-Dayton activities by the HDZ? Do you remember supporting that position? In this article, about halfway down, it says: "Veso Vegar, adviser to Bosnia Croat Presidency member Ante Jelavic, says he also supports the possibility of withdrawing credentials to the two men." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I here must --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does it accurately state your position in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall whether this opinion of mine was credibly relayed and whether I spoke to anybody from Associated Press. I can confirm, though, that there were --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's turn to P 10827 and ask if you remember talking again to Agence France-Presse. 10827. It should be the immediately-preceding document, the 2nd of March, 2001, the second paragraph: "Led by the national Croat -- nationalist Croat Democratic Union HDZ, some 600 Bosnian Croat officials will be asked to sign on to a document on setting up a new council made up of Croats, said Veso Vegar, adviser to HDZ leaders. "An inter-regional council made up of areas where a Croat majority would probably be established, Vegar said, adding that such a council would have its own parliament and government." Did you make that statement or a statement like that in March 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March of that year, it is true that Croatian Peoples Congress was held, but none of this that had been announced to -- that was supposed to happen after that congress, no institutions of executive power, no government was established. I did issue statements, but whether this was my statement and whether it was credibly relayed, I don't know; although, I could have issued a statement that there will be an inter-regional committee. It was announced in all the media and there's no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At the end of that article, it says that: "Mr. Jelavic's criticism escalated at a rally Wednesday in support of Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez who have been sentenced to prison by the UN war crimes tribunal for their role in the massacre of hundreds of Muslims between 1991 and 1994." I'm just wondering, sir, did you attend that same rally with Mr. Jelavic?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you ever attend any rally like that on behalf of any Croats indicted by the ICTY, or attend any fund raisers for their defence, for example?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall I've ever done so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And it was this same Mr. Jelavic that was then removed, because of these activities, removed from the Bosnian, BiH Presidency by the Office of the High Representative because of his anti-Dayton activities later in -- I think later in the same month of March 2001, or if not, then certainly by April; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was removed from the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you continue to be a close adviser to Mr. Jelavic after that time?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, "close associate"? Well, yes, I maintained contacts with Jelavic for several months afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you continue to be an adviser to him in any capacity after he was removed from his position?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, formally I could not be his adviser, because I also resigned my post in the Presidency. It was only logical, because I no longer had anyone to advise there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What post did you hold in the Presidency at that time?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adviser for culture and education.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you held that position as a part of Mr. Jelavic's government, if you will?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, at the BiH Presidency, while he was a Croat member of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you're saying when he was removed, you also left that position; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 10 or 15 days afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can go, sir, to Exhibit P 04626 in the first binder, turning to a different topic, P 04626. It may not -- if it's not in the binder, I think it was used yesterday by the Defence, so again I might have to ask for the assistance of the e-court. My apologies. It was in one of the Defence bundles, P 04626. It is the -- it may not be that we even need it. It's so fresh in everyone's mind that perhaps the courtroom will remember. Sir, this was the HVO IPD document which was dated the 17th -- my apologies, which was document number -- issue number 59, which you told the courtroom you thought it was a bad joke. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very bad joke.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when do you recall first having seen that document?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document, a bulletin, number 59. I saw some -- I read some, but I could not read all of them, and I can't recall when I saw this first. I really can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me explore it with you, sir. It obviously -- according to what you've told us in the courtroom, you suggest that it made quite an impact on you. You thought it was improper. Provided you read it at the time, what action, if any, did you take to respond to this IPD officer who was in your chain of command, to the effect of, "Hey, that's not really appropriate, take some action about that"?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've already noticed this, that the Prosecutor claimed that this was an IPD document. No, this is a document of the OZ South-East Herzegovina, as it's stated here, so it should be precisely stated, so in terms of hierarchy and what the witness could have done about it in the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel. Your Honours, it was covered in the testimony on the first day, or maybe yesterday -- yesterday, at pages 19 and 21, Mr. Vegar testified, "I do know the IPD published a document, the Operative Zone of South-East Herzegovina." This is number 59, IPD. And I believe it was Ms. Alaburic who showed us -- among others who may have showed us an organisational chart of IPD, and all those IPD units were subordinate to Mr. Vegar, and I put that as the proposition to him. And that's what leads me to my question -- if I could just finish my submission first, and then I'll sit down. That's why I put to the witness that if he says this is such a bad joke, what action, if any, did he take to deal with it, if he can assist us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will give you two answers. First of all, I did not have this in my hands and I did not read it then. The other thing, I could not have done anything specific and officially against the authors of this bulletin of the IPD of South-East Herzegovina because I could not order them anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you testified yesterday --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you testified yesterday at pages 103 and 104 of the transcript -- you were asked about the chain of command of the IPD, and you gave this answer: "Apart from their own commander, they were in communication with employees of the IPD, IPD personnel at levels superior to their own, up to the assistant chief of the Defence Department Sector for Moral Guidance." That was you, sir, that was you. So the person who issued this document was directly in your chain of command, and if you thought this was such a bad joke, sir, what, if anything, did you do to discipline or correct the person who issued it?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must also say something that I said yesterday. I said that assistant commanders for IPD were subordinated to their commander. Second thing: They were not in my chain of command. There I said in contact, in communication through the operation zone and the sector in the Defence Department. The third thing: I did not read this then. Had I had the powers to command or sanction, I could not do it, because that problem did not reach me. I was not aware of it, and I could not have done anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, because of the time, I only have one more question on that topic, and that is: To your knowledge, if not by you, did you know then or did you ever learn later that the person who issued that press release or document which you say is a bad joke, was that person ever admonished, fired, punished, by any HVO authority on the inappropriateness of his conduct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we can turn to 2D 01316, 2D 01316 in the second binder. Sir, this is a public announcement dated the 12th of June, 1993, and based on some of your answers in the examinations on Monday and Tuesday, I'd like to just ask you a couple of things. In the second paragraph, it says: "There were a few attempts of infantry attacks. These villages find themselves completely surrounded and if forces of UN do not enter those villages soon, there will be mass slaughter and massacre of the civilians." In the -- at the last paragraph -- at the last paragraph of the document, and again we don't have time, unfortunately, to go through all of it, it talks about the same roads used by Muslim women and children to run from Serbs are now full of Croat women and Croat children running from the Muslim knife. Now, do you think that kind of language was intended to have a calming-down influence?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The wording is in keeping with the dramatic situation. I would not have done -- I would have used such words if I had written it, most certainly, but the suggestion was of general threat to the survival of those people in that area, and such grave words should not surprise us at all in the light of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let's turn next to 2D 1309, which was shown to you yesterday, I believe, or perhaps the day before, but in any event the last couple of days. And let me just say, sir, for the record and so that you don't think that I'm not recognising the situation. As I've said before, some of these events, there were indeed some terrible events that happened with Croat victims, which have my complete condemnation. There's no question about that. But if you look, please, sir, at 2D 01309, I asked you earlier, sir, about these so-called "V.V." documents, and these appear to be documents that you prepared or at least put your initials to. And looking at the first one, in the second paragraph, there is, among other things, this language: "Muslim criminals took pleasure in torturing helpless elderly, women, and children --"

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I don't have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise. 2D 1309. Sorry, sir. I thought you had it. It may be in the Stojic -- excuse me, Your Honour, again I was drawing on a couple of these on the Defence binder. My apology. I believe it's in one of the Stojic binders or bundles. While they're doing that, Your Honour, to save -- hopefully save time again, I may also be referring to 2D 00648, which was also used by the Stojic Defence yesterday, I believe, if people want to also be finding that, and I apologise for the additional effort. Do you have 2D 01309 now, sir? Sir? Or in e-court? 2D 01309, do you have it? If I can direct your attention, please, sir, to the second paragraph on the screen in the Croatian language version in front of you. I believe in that paragraph is the phrase: "Muslim criminals took pleasure in torturing helpless elderly, women and children... another Croat from Zuka's unit was murdered by decapitation, after which his head was thrown in the Neretva. "Sefer Halilovic and Rasim Delic, highest commandants of the Muslim army, knew of the massacre and sent cigarettes to those who committed it as a reward." Now, once again, sir, these phrases and this information, first of all, where did you obtain the information? When you issued -- when you prepared this document, where did you get this information that you based it on?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: These information did not come from official sources, but came from a source which I trusted, and unfortunately many information from this report were proven to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the statement that Mr. Halilovic and Mr. Delic knew of the massacre and sent cigarettes to those that committed it as a reward, what's your source of information for that statement?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it from people who managed to flee that area and who saw Mr. Sefer Halilovic in Jablanica at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you wrote this, and then you -- going on down, there's a series of these -- the 25th, there's a second one, there's one for the 24th, one on the -- two on the 24th, perhaps. Again, did you write these with the -- with the concern in mind that they might have an inflammatory effect on those who might receive and read them? Sir?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: My duty was to inform about this tragic event. Of course, one should be mindful of possible consequences, of course, but at the time, at the time when we heard every day news about tragic events, unfortunately such bad news did not have consequences that they would have in normal times. It was just another bad crime, and it did not elicit a reaction of those who were supposed to prevent such crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you go last on this topic to 2 -- also, and I mentioned it a moment ago, if we could find 2D 00648 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, may I ask you two brief questions. How did you know that Halilovic and Delic had thanked the perpetrators of those crimes by giving them cigarettes? How did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard it from people who escaped from that area. They were lucky to be able to escape. They saw Mr. Halilovic several days after the massacre, and that was the story that circulated around Jablanica. At that time, cigarettes were very precious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. So the person who gives the information had seen Mr. Halilovic handing out packs of cigarettes to the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, she only saw Mr. Halilovic, but that was the information that circulated around Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Second question. I can see that you were talking about the women who were in the Museum of the Revolution, where things that you have written may have happened, and I'm not going to -- what is alleged has happened, I'm not going to say that again. Did you grasp what consequences the fact of writing about that would have on families, people who were worried? Did you think about that? In one or the other assumption, either what you write is true or it's not, but in both cases did you grasp the potential consequences it would have on the families, on the neighbours, et cetera, or is it mere propaganda?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My first and foremost aim at the time was to present facts, and I believe that the information is unfortunately true concerning that massacre that happened, but also the camp that existed in Jablanica, detaining mostly civilians, because there were very, very few soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if we can just look briefly --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: 2D 00648, another one that was shown to you previously. Again, sir, it's over your initials, and in part -- this is for the April 16th, and it says: "Over radio connections, they clearly tell Croats that they will be slaughtered and that this will be land 'Muslimanija'." Do you see that? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it on the screen at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I can see it. It's the bottom -- it's the last sentence above your initials "V.V.," sir. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, because our time is so limited, can I just put this to you: Isn't it correct, sir, that all sides, all sides, engaged in propaganda and hate speech and inflammatory language in connection with the events that were going on at the time, including the HVO, including sometimes you, yourself, sir?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say again that I only presented the information and the facts that I received, I put it on paper. There is no expression of my opinion, my comments, or any statements of mine. This word "Muslimanija," was used by the soldiers who looted the houses, burned those villages, not by the person who relayed this information to me. I also did not have that word in my vocabulary, I didn't use it in my reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to go next to -- changing topics, unless the Chamber has any questions on that, I'd like you to go, please, to P 10675 in the second binder. Yes, second binder, P 10675. Sir, this is a compilation -- the Chamber has seen it before -- the courtroom has seen it before -- of four articles all written around early April 1993 -- ones that -- well, three are early, one is the 20th. We have a 4 April article by Reuters. We have a 6th of April article by Agence France-Presse. We have a 7th of April article by the "Christian Science Monitor," and we have a 20 April article by the Financial Times. And I'll just make it very clear to you, sir, that they all deal with certain statements made by the HVO in April of 1993. And let me direct your attention, because time is short, specifically to the 6th April Agence France-Presse article. It will be the second article in your bundle, please. In the third paragraph from the bottom of that article, this statement is made: "A communique published on Monday by the Zagreb daily 'Vijesnik' said the HVO had decided to force the Bosnians to implement the plan, regardless of the Serbs. 'It is definitely an ultimatum,' said HVO spokesman Veso Vegar, adding, 'We cannot wait indefinitely to put the peace plan into practice.'" That's what you told Agence France-Presse; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say this to the Agence France-Presse. I never used, in these statements, the word "ultimatum." And I cross-checked this through the media. The Zagreb "Vijesnik" does not quote that statement of mine or that I gave anyone an ultimatum. All that appeared in those days was a statement from the session of the Croatian Defence Council but during those days I did not give any statements, and I couldn't have given an ultimatum if there hadn't been one from the HVO. I was not in a position to make decisions for someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not suggesting or never intended to suggest that it was your personal ultimatum. It was an ultimatum given by the HVO; correct? And that's what you're addressing; yes?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't have said that, because the HVO that not issued an ultimatum either.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me. Let's look back at the 4 April 1993 Reuters article. About halfway through that article issued in Zagreb on the 4th of April, you'll find this statement: "'If Izetbegovic fails to sign this agreement by April 15, the HVO will unilaterally enforce its jurisdiction in cantons 3, 8 and 10,' the statement from HVO headquarters in the south-west Croat stronghold of Mostar warned. Croatian Radio said, 'Bosnian Croat chieftain Mate Boban had already signed the proposed communique and the president's signature was ''expected'' ..."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you mind reading slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies, interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't that -- when someone says, If this doesn't happen, something else is going to happen. Now, the word "ultimatum" might not appear in that particular passage, but isn't that exactly what it is? If you don't do this, we are going to do this. That's the definition of "ultimatum," isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in my understanding. But I have to say again, I'm not here to interpret the positions expressed at the session of the HVO. I understood that there was no ultimatum, and in my statements I could not have said to anyone that the Croats would do this and that if somebody does not withdraw, or that we would do anything to make them withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let's go to the 7 April 1993 "Christian Science Monitor" article, the third article in the bundle, the "Christian Science Monitor" for the 7th of April. The third paragraph from the -- no, forgive me, it's a longer article. You will see, sir, and I'll simply read it to you, and I will read slowly - for the English readers, it's at the bottom of the first page - there's this paragraph, sir. I'll read two paragraphs to you: "But Jadranko Prlic, the self-styled acting prime minister of 'Herceg-Bosna,' says the ultimatum reflects only HVO's intention to implement the demilitarisation clause of the Vance-Owen Plan. 'We signed the document and the Muslims signed the document, and it is one of the real ways to overcome problems between Muslims and Croats,' he says. "Mr. Prlic concedes, nonetheless, that the HVO ultimatum could lead to bloodshed. 'We expect everything. We don't want this struggle. We don't have any reason for this struggle,' he says." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is that an accurate statement of the HVO position at the time, at least in part?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware at that time that that was the HVO's general position. I did not understand it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, I put it to you that in the Agence France-Presse article that I put to you initially, and your statements about this being an ultimatum, "it is definitely an ultimatum," I put it to you, sir, that Agence France-Presse got it exactly right, and that is indeed what you said at the time, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, several months ago we saw this document, and I had put the question to the witness then. You are a professional. You know the AFP, you know the Reuters agency. You must know that when a quote is given of a sentence, that means that the sentence was said by someone. Now, this regards you, because you are being mentioned in this story. If I understand properly, there was a press release issued on Monday by the Zagreb newspaper "Vjesnik" in which those sentences were quoted, so I suppose you are at the origin of this press release. The Agence France-Presse only relays something that was published in "Vjesnik"; is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said that I spoke to "Vjesnik," but "Vjesnik" did not carry an ultimatum. It only relayed the information from the session of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of assistance, please. We have that "Vjesnik" issue of the 5th to which this article refers. It contains neither the communique, nor the statement. If you wish, if the Trial Chamber allows, we can provide this issue and put it in e-court during the break. There's nothing to translate. There is no communique and no statement in the "Vjesnik" issue of the 5th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you were ahead of me. You knew what question I wanted to put to Mr. Scott. I wanted to ask him how it was that the Prosecution did not try to find that newspaper to check that, and the Defence just told us that they have the press cutting and that the quotes are not present in that communique, so now it's on the transcript. Mr. Scott, you have a few minutes before the break. In terms of time, I'll tell you soon how much time you have left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you very much. I would appreciate it, so that I can review and determine the use of the rest of my time. Your Honour, I'd also remind the Chamber, with great respect, that there was also additional direct examination time taken by several of the other accused, and of course I will ask that that time be included in the time that I have, since the Prosecution gets the same amount as direct examination, I believe. So if the Registrar can assist us both in that respect, it would be much appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honours. My examination was under three hours, if I am not mistaken, and since cross-examination is proportionate to direct examination, I'm just giving this as a reminder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm certainly in the hands of the Registrar and I will abide -- absolutely strictly abide by any numbers that they come up with. May I -- THE COURT: I'm going to tell you. You have 49 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I have 49 minutes based -- the Stojic Defence took, as I understood it, three hours and ten minutes. I also understand that both the Praljak Defence and one of the other Defence teams took direct examination time, so I'll ask the Registrar to please assist us in determining how much additional direct examination time was also taken by the other co-accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, the quality of Prosecution or Defence is not the time it takes, it is the quality of the questions that are put. In the matter of a few minutes, you can raise a fundamental issue. You can also spend hours on nothing. We're going to have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. Let's take stock of the situation. Mr. Scott, you are entitled to additional time because Ms. Pinter took 15 minutes to address new issues, so you should make due with 10 minutes. So all in all, you'll have 59 minutes. There's under an hour until the end of the hearing. I guess that Ms. Nozica may have some redirect; I don't know at all. It all hinges on you. If you act swiftly and efficiently, we can finish today. Otherwise, everybody will have to be back tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may just, for the transcript, I think it must be recorded in the transcript that Mr. Pusic has not attended the session since the break before this one, since after the first break he has suffered from heavy back pain and was allowed to return. I think it must be reflected in the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. I thought it was not necessary to record this on the transcript, in as much as the accused was present at the beginning of the hearing. He is represented by his counsel, and if he has to leave the courtroom due to medical reasons, there's no need to have it on the record. But this being said, each of the Judges having stated their views, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and I do appreciate the time. I will try to move as quickly as possible. I represent to the Chamber that even over the break, I made substantial adjustments in my outline, so I'm hopeful.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to next show you before moving on to the next topic, and I would like to have this distributed, P 10850, for the record, but I'm distributing it -- with the usher's assistance, I'm distributing it now. Apparently it didn't find its way in the binders. I'm sure it's probably my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: The name didn't make it to the transcript either, so if you would repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: One -- excuse me, P 10850. Thank you, Judge. P 10850. It's also available in the e-court, if that assists anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir -- I think everyone has it. Sir, this appears to be a document that was put out over your name, "Veso Vegar." On the top of the first page, we have handwritten: "Received on 11 August 1993." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And this is a document that you prepared, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, this is directed to the attention "All is assistants for IPD and brigades, Uskoplje, Novi Travnik, Rama, or Prozor, Skopje also of course being Gornji Vakuf, Kiseljak, and Vitez, so in light of the discussion we had earlier today I'm going to suggest to you that this was a distribution from you to IPD assistants in the field, which would not be surprising, correct, because you're communicating to people in your structure?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm addressing assistants for IPD in these brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, our time as you heard is very limited. In the second paragraph of the document you'll see: "It should be openly stated ..." But then you go on to say: "We have to strongly confront all troublemakers, all those, which are spreading defeatism and even panic, and not even run from their isolation. "Urgently put out of action 'all knowing' gentlemen, those that spread rumours about 'sold out' this and that, and this or that town was given away to Muslims or Serbs. The leadership of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna ... gave nothing away." And so on. Are those your words, sir?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was the context in which this document was prepared, please?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of massive disinformation and rumours, that someone on behalf of the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna had sold out, namely, agreed to the hand-over of certain towns to be given to another, to a second or a third republic, this document was created after the third agreement that envisaged a union. That's why it says in the first sentence that we have now received our own republic, but within Bosnia and Herzegovina. And now smart-alecks appear, know-it-alls who disperse such information that they got from not only Croats, but also from the second or the third side, and they spread chaos in the minds of people. This information had the objective of changing the prevailing sentiment and refuting such rumours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I only have time to point one other part of it to you, unless of course the Judges have questions, but in the next paragraph that begins under the words: "Honourable HVO soldier ...," there is this statement: "We will not agree on any rotten compromises and proposals like the one by Alija Izetbegovic on joint state from Neum to the Sava river." What rotten compromise were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think for people who lived in that area, it was understandable, what I was trying to say. I was talking about a political concept, an idea that can be characterized as unitaristic, with a strong centralisation of power in one place, that is to say, Sarajevo, wherein none of the three ethnic communities in Bosnia and Herzegovina would have been separate or able to develop their own separate identity. This sentence does not mean that I was denying that state. It means that Croats agreed to such a state, but that they should have their own separate identity within that state. And, anyway, this agreement did envisage three entities within one state.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And that was a separate Croat entity with a separate territory set aside for Croats; correct? According to you?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It envisaged a separate republic where the Croats would be a majority, just like the other two republics where the Serbs and Muslims respectively would be the majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is, yes, there would be a separate entity and separate territory for Croats; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, we have to move on to Exhibit, please, P 10837, P 10837 in the second binder. And I'm turning to the topic of events in Mostar in May and June 1993. Sir, this is an article from the Associated Press, dated 11 May 1993. And I'm going to have to move rather quickly, sir, and I'm going to put statements attributed to you in this article. Once again, I'm sure that if I misquote or misstate, I'll be corrected. But in this article, and it's on the second page of the English version, I'll read it very slowly, sir, this statement is attributed to you: "Vegar said civilians of all ethnic groups were merely being evacuated from combat zones." And that was in response to UN officials, two paragraphs up, if you will: "UN officials said they were concerned about Muslim civilians reportedly cleared out of their homes in Mostar on Sunday. "'There have been a number of civilians taken from their homes,' said a US Army captain... 'We assume they are being detained or being taken out of the area against their will.'" And then in that context, sir, it's attributed to you: "Vegar said civilians of all ethnic groups were merely being evacuated from gather zones." And before putting a question to you about that, can I just ask you to turn very close by, P 10845. It should be just a couple of documents down in your binder, P 10845. This is an article from -- on the 12th of May, 1993, the following day, from the "Seattle Post-Intelligencer." Yet again -- sorry, sir, let me just point out, at the bottom of that, the English page, the first page of the article -- excuse me: "When asked about the evidence of civilian detentions Croat military spokesman --"

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not getting any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies. I'll start again, and please tell us: "When asked about the evidence ..." Are you getting translation? "When asked about the evidence --"

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Maybe it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, I'm sorry, but it is probably you might want to mention that it is on page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Prandler. I think perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness is saying there is no translation. He means the paper, the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, there is not a translation of this. That's why I'm reading it to you, sir, which is not a new procedure. It's a procedure we've followed for the last three years: "When asked about the evidence of civilian detentions, Croat military spokesman Veso Vegar said civilians of all ethnic groups were being evacuated from combat zones."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, where did you form the opinion or form the position that what was happening to the Muslims in early May 1993 was an evacuation for their own safety? Did you come up with that on your own or is that what someone else told you?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That evacuation did have the purpose to ensure their safety, especially in war-affected zones, and that was all of Mostar because that was a small town. But as far as I know, the first to be evacuated were the streets closest to combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, my question was, and I apologise if it wasn't clear or if it wasn't -- there was a problem in translation, but our time is short: Is that a position that you formed and stated on your own or is that a position that was the HVO position at the time? Were you stating that as your -- in your capacity as spokesperson for the HVO Department of Defence, and if so, who confirmed that position to you? Who said, "This is our position"?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody told me it was our position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, that statement is just completely wrong, isn't it, because it wasn't all civilians, all ethnic groups -- civilians of all ethnic groups being evacuated; it was specifically only Muslims, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still maintain that all the people who were in the immediate danger of war were evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And they just happened to be only Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were not only Muslims, although Muslims were the majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, are you aware, sir, that this Tribunal has found, in fact, and this Trial Chamber has so ruled on adjudicated facts, that this effort was directed only at Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry. I object on the basis that the Prosecutor is leading evidence that is not admitted here in this trial, in the sense that he is trying to make it out. I invite the Prosecutor to check the lists from Heliodrom that he tendered himself and to check how many Serbs and Croats there are on the lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- I'll refer to the adjudicated fact in this case, number 91, as issued by this Trial Chamber: "The arrest and detention of the civilian population in Mostar was carried out on a discriminatory basis, as the Bosnian Muslim population was targeted specifically, while their Croat neighbours were left unharmed. It was unlawful, since there was no legal basis for this measure." That's the adjudicated fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, it wasn't --

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. I would like to remind the Prosecutor of the status of adjudicated facts; namely, that they can be disproven, and the Prosecutor has himself led evidence in the form of these lists where it is obvious that there are Serbs and Croats and others on those lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me be very clear, sir. So you're saying the statement that the Muslims were being evacuated for their own safety and that this was happening to all ethnic groups, this is something that Veso Vegar, completely by himself, when the question was put, it was completely your position, the answer you gave, without consultation with anyone else in the HVO authorities or Mr. Stojic, your superior; is that what you're telling the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, I'm sure I didn't contact anyone, although it was not only my position; it was the position shared by many others. That's why I put it, then and now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you go, please, to Exhibit P 10838 in the second binder. P 10838. Sir, this is a document -- this is a report from Reuters on the 14th of May, 1993, titled "Croat Troops Free Some Muslim Detainees in Mostar." Apparently on that day, the second paragraph: "Fifty women, children, and elderly were taken by bus from the helicopter complex where they had been interned after being removed from their home in the city on Sunday." Skipping to -- one, two -- the third paragraph below that, it says: "HVO spokesman, Veso Vegar, said all the Muslims would be free once Croats arrested by Bosnian Army troops in the Jablanica-Konjic pocket north-east of Mostar were released." Now, again, the position is stated that the HVO would free the others detained at the Heliodrom once Croats arrested and held by Bosnian Army troops elsewhere were released. Who formed that position and communicated that to you, or was this again Veso Vegar acting as the leader of the HVO and making that decision on your own?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I spoke to this subject at all, I could only have talked about detained Muslim soldiers, certainly not those who were evacuated from Mostar, so I think there's nothing illogical if I linked the release of prisoners on one side with the release of prisoners on the other side because at that time, in Konjic and Jablanica, there were many Croats detained, fighting men, but also civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this is a very central issue to these proceedings. You are saying that if the Muslims who were arrested can be released -- well, they can be released if the Croats that were arrested in the Jablanica-Konjic area are released as well. The problem is that -- well, I'm not aware of the situation in Jablanica-Konjic. I don't know which Croats were arrested. But if there were Croat civilians arrested in Jablanica, due to this sort of dual track, the Muslims arrested in Mostar could also be civilians. Can you see the extent of your statements then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can look it up, but I'm not talking about the capture of civilians in order to exchange them for some other civilians in Jablanica and Konjic. I am certain that I am talking here only about imprisoned soldiers and their possible exchange. But I always referred to the freedom of movement for civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're now speaking about military, but in this Reuters statement, there's no distinction between civilians and military, just mention is made of Croats and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the agency did not distinguish between fighting men and civilians, but I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, that's not entirely true, sir. If you look at the first sentence of the article Reuters says: "Bosnian forces on Friday released about 50 of 2.000 Muslim civilians detained in squalid conditions outside of Mostar as sporadic fighting persisted around the south-western Bosnian city." But my specific -- I persist in my question to you originally, sir, I put it to you: This was not Veso Vegar's only single decision, this was a policy statement or decision taken, a strategy announced by the HVO, and unless you were in a much more senior position than the one you were in, that wasn't your decision, sir, about when other people would be released. Now, who told you that was the HVO policy or situation -- excuse me, strategy, that when people -- when Croats in Konjic would be released, then civilians being held at the Heliodrom would be released? Who told you that was the position?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fully agree this was not my decision, whether 50 would be released or all of them. I did not discuss that at all and I did not take decisions, but pursuant to the erstwhile practice, I discuss the process of exchange which would always take place after decisive events where there would be more captured soldiers. I'm sure I spoke about the soldiers, not civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the evictions of Muslims in Mostar continued throughout the balance of May, and when I say "the balance," after the 10th of May, 1993, and continuing through June and thereafter; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Muslims, Croats and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, sir. The eviction of Muslim families and Muslims continued throughout Mostar, in West Mostar, throughout the balance of May, June and July; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all subsequent months, but not only of the Muslims, as I said. I can give you reliable data that in the eastern --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will direct your attention to P 02557. I apologise for cutting you off, but the Chamber -- we only have so much time. P 02557.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It should not be broadcast, I'm told, Your Honour. We can use it in the courtroom, but the document itself should not be broadcast outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, but I've been listening to the Croatian interpretation. What I'm bothered about - maybe my English is not good enough - but in the headphones we heard, and I think this is important, the moving out as interpretation for the word "eviction." I'm not sure that's the most fortuitous choice of words when the witness is asked questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I can't -- unfortunately, I can't control the exact translations of my words. I did use -- I believe I used the words "eviction" and "expulsion," and those are the words I intend to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you look at P 02557, sir, this is a report dated 29th of May, 1993. Item number 6 --

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise to my learned friend Scott. The key thing happened again while I rose. Now the witness received the word "protivanje," [phoen] "expulsion," which is something completely different from that, when -- what he heard when Mr. Scott discussed "evictions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Witness, the Prosecutor in English used the word "eviction." In your language, what did you understand? What was it that was translated to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood that he was talking about moving out, temporary leaving the town of Mostar, and this is the context that I spoke in, people fleeing war and war threat, but not on a permanent basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean, if the whole record now for the last 15 minutes is contaminated by confusion, then it's -- we've lost the time and I can't -- I'm not going to be held hostage by the loss of time on that. The specific word that I've used repeatedly is "eviction" and "expulsion," and that's what the documents use. So it's to my prejudice, I'm afraid, but look at, sir, P 02557, item 6: "Both the UNHCR and the ICRC report the internment and eviction of Muslims in Mostar and the towns of the south ..." Skipping a line or two: "The UNHCR and the ICRC say report that Muslim families on the west bank were evicted last night in organised raids, their homes occupied by Croat families with 'permits' to occupy the flats. In addition to families which were squatting in homes vacated by Serbs, regular residents were also evicted." Now, as I said, that kind of eviction, that expulsion, was going on through May, June, and July, Muslims being evicted from West Mostar; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that there were individual cases of people coming into flats and evicting the inhabitants from those flats, on the part of criminal and uncontrolled groups, but I cannot accept the statement which is being put forward here, that this was done by official institutions, that it was done by the HVO or a unit of the HVO. Simply, there was no plan of expulsion or of ethnic cleansing of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's go to P 02538, P 02538. Sir, this is a document issued -- a communique issued by Mr. Maric on the 27th of May, 1993, in connection with flats in Mostar. Quote in the first paragraph: "Pursuant to a verbal order issued by the head of the HZ Herceg-Bosna Defence Department," I put it to you the head of that is Mr. Stojic, "... with the aim of providing necessary accommodation for family members of soldiers from the Ludwig Pavlovic Regiment," et cetera, it's a communication, "the comission hereby places ten apartments at disposal allegedly previously owned by the JNA." Now, this has been copied to -- you'll see that this has been distributed to the head of the Defence Department, Mr. Stojic, and several other persons. Now, sir, if you will keep that document in mind --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honours, I must object to this. Mr. Scott must bring into connection those flats with what he was asking the witness about previously. He seems to be implying that somebody had been dislocated from those flats. He must lay the grounds, prove that the decree on the attribution of flats was taken, there were criteria that were applied, and this has nothing to do with this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Nozica, there's no reason to say that. You've got professional Judges here who have been dealing with this case for three years. For 24 hours a day -- 20 hours a day we're dealing with this case, we're hearing this case. So you can easily imagine that when Mr. Scott talks about it, we are all focused on this, and so it's pointless to tell us, yes -- well, we'll see. Wait and the see the rest of the question. Yes, Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED STOJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. You know, I've been sitting here for three years, and I've been silent so far, but this is very difficult for me to suffer, because that person over there is airing lies. I'm responsibly saying this. This document has nothing to do with what Mr. Scott is talking about, no connection. Your Honours, I cannot suffer this any longer. You must understand us. There used to be six of us here. Now there are only two of us remaining. I cannot suffer this any longer. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojic, the Judges have a document which mentions apartments occupied by the JNA that are going to be made at the disposal. Now, it's up to the Prosecutor to establish the connection between the apartments, Muslims who may have occupied the apartments and who may have vacated them, for Mr. Serafinov [phoen], Pesic, [indiscernible] and so on. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we can go to Exhibit P 02756, P 02756 in the first binder. This is an ECMM report dated the 14th of June, 1993. I'll direct your attention, Mr. Vegar, to paragraph number -- item number 6, "Other matters."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Skipping a few lines, it says: "We have got information from three different sources about, again since Saturday afternoon, Muslim families are being expelled by HVO soldiers from their homes via south-east quarter Donja Mahala, to the east bank. Approximately more than 100 Muslim people were Sunday night and today expelled from the quarters Dum and Patikana [phoen]. On most of their apartments, there were HVO stickers found where the apartments were occupied by HVO soldiers." Item 6, "Assessment," the second item: "The ethnic cleansing on the west bank of Muslim families by the HVO still goes on." That's what was happening at the time; correct, sir? Muslims were being -- Muslim families were being thrown out, HVO soldiers were moving in; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, this is the first time I've seen this document. I have to go through it. I see that General Pasalic sent a protest note.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That wasn't my question, sir. That's what -- these evictions were what was going on in June and July of 1993, and you were aware of it, weren't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- what I knew about this, I already told you. I maintain that HVO units did not do so. Individuals did that, most probably civilians wearing uniforms. Everybody was wearing uniforms in Mostar at the time. They had no other clothes. I cannot tell you or know whether there were any HVO soldiers among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's look at Exhibit P 03179 in the first binder, P 03179. Sir, this is an HVO military police report for the 3rd of July, 1993. I would like to direct your attention, please, to the headings which are -- it gives by zone, and if you can find the part of the report under zone number 2. Then there are three numbered -- there are three names with numbers, 1, 2, 3, and I will begin at the next paragraph after the third name.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to my learned friend Scott. May I remind Their Honours that on several occasions, and this has been accepted as an exhibit and we stick by our objection, that this document does not bear the signature of the alleged author, nor the stamp, and nor the letterhead which is usual for military police communications. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: From 2000 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a second. Madam -- let me reply to the lawyer. Counsel, okay, you challenged this report. Fine. You see that this report is signed by somebody named [indiscernible]. Why not summon here -- here with other witnesses for him to say, "I've never written this document"?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we move into private session or closed session, please, for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, look, we'll deal with this at some other point. We have very little time left. Mr. Scott, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, it says: "From 2000 to 2200 hours, eviction of refugees from the Pupils' Hostel was carried out. They were taken to the left riverbank. There were 310 persons. From 2230 to 2330 hours, the eviction from the kindergarten in Liska Street was carried out and the persons were taken to the left riverbank. There were 36 persons. Regular patrolling duty was performed during the night." Those were Muslims being evicted from the west bank to the east side; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know of these events. Particularly, not -- I can't believe that there was mass evictions of this sort. This is the first time I've seen the document, and I don't know anything about the pupils' dormitory. I can't recall this at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, we don't have time to go through every single document I might put in front of you on this topic, but I do want it to be very clear. Your position is, and what you're telling these Judges, under oath, is that you were not aware of the mass eviction of Muslims from West Mostar taking place from the 10th -- from 9th of May, through the rest of May, into June, into July, and thereafter of 1993; you're telling these Judges you didn't know that was going on?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not have any information, neither do I recall any mass expulsion. I remember and I said that there were individual cases, repeated several times, but I don't know of any thought-out plan or design about mass expulsions. That, I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's go to Exhibit P 10846, P 10846, second line. Sir, this is a Agence France-Presse article from the 9th of June, 1993, concerning the movement of Muslims in Mostar. It attributes this statement to you, in quotation marks: "'We (Croats) are doing their (the Serbs') job now,' Vegar said with a smile." What Serb job were the Croats doing in early June 1993?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a terrible lie. I must protest. I've never heard such a terrible lie in this courtroom, that I allegedly said that we were doing the Serbs' job. No, I never would say that, and I never did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The third paragraph: "The Croats are now trying to convince the Muslims remaining on the west side to leave, but foreign sources say the residents are so intermingled that the operation is proving problematical." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall a single such sentence. I'm not sure whether this is anybody's statement or whether this was just a conclusion of the author, the journalist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very quickly, sir, very briefly. Now, if this journalist states that you smiled, it's probably that he saw you. So did you meet with this journalist on the 9th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I cannot recall which journalist I met on which day, but it's impossible that I've said that, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you'll allow me, I'm sorry for this interruption, but even if we did say they -- let's see how this is written. Those are obviously not the words of Mr. Vegar, if we take a look at what is attributed. Why do we have "Croats" and "Serbs" in brackets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have the translation, so I can't really tell you what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Ms. Nozica, I'll give you credit for what you're saying.
