It's quite surprising that a journalist, who is supposed to faithfully give the words of a person, should put in between brackets these words and interpret those words. I've never seen that up until now. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I just inquire from the Registrar --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies. Could I inquire of the Registry, please, as to the time-limits, because given what time I have left, I mean, I've just -- I've pushed as fast as I could, but I think it's unrealistic to think we'll be finished by 1.45. If the Registry can assist me, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the main issue is whether Ms. Nozica has additional questions in redirect.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will have five to ten minutes, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So we won't have the five to ten minutes. Mr. Scott, theoretically you have 26 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to turn to the topic of convoys, and I'd like to start, please, if I could direct your attention to P 10831 in this second -- excuse me -- yes, the second binder, P 10831. Sir, this is a Reuters article dated the 1st of March, 1993. The first lead-in sentence says: "Bosnian Croat forces said on Monday they were enforcing a blockade of supply convoys for their estranged Muslim allies, despite Bosnian government reports that it had been lifted." I'm going to skip a paragraph. This statement is attributed to you, sir, so you're on notice: "'We're stopping all Bosnia-Herzegovina army convoys with military equipment and weapons and any kind of supplies headed for areas where there is tension or outright fighting between the HVO and Muslims,' HVO spokesman Veso Vegar told Reuters. "Bosnian Army columns destined for regions where HVO and Muslim forces were jointly battling the Serbs, such as in north-east Bosnia around Tuzla, were being allowed to pass." Now, the statement attributed to you, sir, is that an accurate statement as what was happening in the 1st of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall what was going on precisely on the 1st of March, and I'm sorry about that, but I can tell you about the information about the stopping of convoys. There were such cases, yes. Very often in convoys containing humanitarian aid, weapons, munitions, military equipment, were being transported, and of course somebody had to have control over such convoys because very often -- well, so that we could know who is carrying weapons for whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, again because of the shortness of time, I simply want to know. Was it -- did you accurately state the HVO position at the time, that BiH Army convoys with military equipment and weapons and any kind of supplies headed for areas where there is tension or outright fighting between the HVO and Muslims were being stopped? Is that an accurate statement by you of the HVO's position during this time-period?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If those convoys were stopped then to be examined, that was the HVO's position. Of course, the HVO did that, not me. I could just relay information if such things were happening at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, if you could go, please, to 10832. Perhaps we'll have time to finish one more document today. P 10832. Sir, this is a Reuters article by -- excuse me, the 24th of August, 1993, again about a convoy, but this is about a different situation. This concerns a humanitarian convoy to Mostar. I'll give people a chance to scan down a bit. Nineteen trucks -- about halfway through the article, sir, this statement is attributed to you, or this position or information is attributed to you: "Croat military spokesman Veso Vegar said the convoy would be given safe conduct through Croat check-points into the Muslim quarter of the divided city later on Tuesday or Wednesday." Then it goes on to say: "'Some of its cargo would be unloaded in Croat-controlled Central Mostar as the price of passage,' he said. "'The HVO (Bosnian-Croat forces) will let the convoy through later today or tomorrow, despite the fact that 190.000 Croats are under siege by Muslims in Central Bosnia,' Vegar told Reuters by telephone from Mostar in South-West Bosnia." Now, did you make -- did you provide that sort of information? I'm not going to say -- I'm not going to hold you, sir, to the exact words stated here, but do you remember providing such information to Reuters and other journalists around the 24th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If on that day a convoy planned for Mostar was -- Eastern Mostar was scheduled, then I can confirm that I had given that information. And the second statement, that part of the cargo would be unloaded as the price of passage, I can tell you that I never heard of such a price for humanitarian convoys, I never received information that parts of the cargo for humanitarian convoy would be taken and the other part being let through. I don't know anything about that, and no such information reached me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that will have to finish us for the day, with the Court's permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you want to continue. You still have 20 minutes. You want to continue tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, you shall have to return tomorrow. Ms. Nozica will address questions in redirect tomorrow. Mr. Coric's counsel can say tomorrow what she wanted to say today. She should remind me so that I can give her the floor tomorrow. It's quarter to. We have to stop because there's the Popovic case sitting here after us. Have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of February, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
